Let the cube have center at \(O=(0,0,0)\) and vertices \((\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)\).

For a cube vertex with sign vector \(v=(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3)\), the plane through its three adjacent vertices has equation
\[
\varepsilon_1 x+\varepsilon_2 y+\varepsilon_3 z=1.
\]
The center \(O\) lies on the side where
\[
\varepsilon_1 x+\varepsilon_2 y+\varepsilon_3 z\le 1.
\]
Requiring this for all eight choices of signs is equivalent to
\[
|x|+|y|+|z|\le 1.
\]
This inequality describes a regular octahedron. Its six vertices are
\[
(\pm1,0,0),\quad(0,\pm1,0),\quad(0,0,\pm1),
\]
which are the centers of the six faces of the original cube. Its eight triangular faces lie in the eight cutting planes. Also \(O\) is strictly inside this piece, not on any cutting plane, so it belongs to one unique piece.

Therefore the central piece is the octahedron, choice A.

\[
\boxed{\text{A (a regular octahedron)}}
\]
